summary: The change makes TypeCollector defensive for metadata-declared members: it stops indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] (which threw IndexOutOfRangeException for types from referenced assemblies) and skips compiler-generated/non-referenceable fields, so the generator no longer crashes (no CS8785) and emits a resolver, and the analyzer no longer throws (no AD0001). All three new tests pass on head and two fail on base with the exact IndexOutOfRangeException at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo, indicating root-cause coverage. Separately, the change flips MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.HashCollisionResistant from true to false - an out-of-scope security regression that fails five runtime security tests - and should not merge as-is.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: All three new tests pass on head asserting no generator exception, no CS8785, and a GeneratedMessagePackResolver; on base source two of them fail with IndexOutOfRangeException at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo caused by indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].

evidence.quote: this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(Diagnostic.Create(MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull, item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() is PropertyDeclarationSyntax propertySyntax ? propertySyntax.Identifier.GetLocation() : item.Locations.FirstOrDefault(), formattedType.ToDisplayString(SymbolDisplayFormat.FullyQualifiedFormat), item.Name));

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: The same three tests pass on head asserting no analyzer exceptions and no AD0001 diagnostics; the two base failures show the analyzer path crashed on the same IndexOutOfRangeException.

The crash-prone DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing was replaced with safe navigation and a Locations fallback (head lines 985, 1080), and the analyzer runs without exceptions, but no test inspects diagnostic Location values for metadata-declared members, so I cannot verify that no diagnostic is reported at a location outside the app compilation.
The full source-generator suite passes with 170/170 and no failures, versus 167/167 on base, so no existing diagnostics regressed.
The fail_without_fix check passed: 2 of the 3 new tests fail on base source, so the fix is covered by automated tests that fail without it.

findings.title: UntrustedData no longer hash-collision resistant
findings.claim: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.HashCollisionResistant was changed from true (base line 37) to false (head line 37), so UntrustedData dictionaries fall back to EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of collision-resistant comparers. This library deserializes untrusted input, and the runtime suite fails five security tests: EqualityComparer_CollisionResistance_Guid, EqualityComparer_CollisionResistance_Int64, EqualityComparer_ObjectFallback_UnsupportedType, TypelessFormatterWithUntrustedData_UnsafeKeys, Untrusted. The change is also unrelated to issue #2283.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs to HashCollisionResistant = true for UntrustedData. If the SipHash cost is a real concern, submit it as a separate change with a security review and benchmarks.

findings.title: MessagePackSecurity edit is out of scope for issue #2283
findings.claim: The MessagePackSecurity.cs edit addresses hashing performance on hot paths, not the generator/analyzer crash on closed generic value types from referenced assemblies. No requirement clause covers hashing configuration, and the runtime security failures show it is not a safe change to bundle in.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs from this change; re-submit it separately with security sign-off.

findings.title: New tests do not assert the guarded behavior
findings.claim: Mutation testing failed: 4 mutants survived at the two changed lines (TypeCollector.cs 985 and 1050), and 0 of 2 mutated hunks have a killed mutant. Removing the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic call (M1) still passes, and weakening or dropping the field-skip guard (M2-M4) still passes. The tests assert no crash/no CS8785/no AD0001 but never assert that a diagnostic is produced when it should be, or that compiler-generated fields from metadata assemblies are skipped, so the fix's correctness is not locked in and REQ-2283-F3 (diagnostic locations) is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add assertions for expected diagnostics (e.g. BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for a member with neither key kind) and verify resolver output; add a metadata-lib case with an auto-property so the backing-field guard is exercised by a failing-on-base test.

findings.title: Inconsistent null-location fallback for field diagnostics
findings.claim: The property-side BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic (head line 985) falls back to item.Locations.FirstOrDefault() when DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty, but the field-side equivalent (head line 1131) uses FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() with no fallback and can produce a null location. Both are crash-safe, but inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same ?? item.Locations.FirstOrDefault() fallback at line 1131 for consistency.

refusals.topic: Whether the SipHash performance trade-off for UntrustedData is acceptable
refusals.reason: No benchmarks or performance measurements were provided, so the commit message's hot-path claim cannot be verified from the evidence, and accepting a weaker security posture for untrusted deserialization is a security-owner decision, not a reviewer one.
